summary.text: Laura Gillen is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 4th Congressional District, which includes Nassau County's South Shore. A Nassau County attorney, she served as Hempstead Town Supervisor from 2018 to 2020, lost the 2022 race for this seat, and won it in 2024. She serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

paragraphs.text: Gillen was born on July 10, 1969, in Rockville Centre, New York, and grew up in Baldwin; her House biography describes her as a Baldwin native.
She graduated from Sacred Heart Academy, then earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from Georgetown University in 1991, where she was a George Baker Scholar.
After college she volunteered during the AIDS crisis and at Mother Teresa's Home for the Dying in Kolkata, according to her House biography.
Gillen attended Georgetown Law Center before earning a J.D. from New York University School of Law in 2000.

She worked as a litigator at Cahill Gordon & Reindel, including pro bono work representing victims of domestic violence, and from 2005 at the Nassau County firm Westerman Ball Ederer Miller Zucker & Sharfstein.

She was elected Hempstead Town Supervisor in 2017, becoming the first Democrat in over a century to hold the office (her official biography says in 112 years), and served from 2018 to 2020; she lost her 2019 re-election bid to Donald X. Clavin Jr.
Gillen ran for NY-4 in 2022, winning the Democratic primary but losing the general election to Anthony D'Esposito.
She defeated D'Esposito in the 2024 rematch and was sworn in on January 3, 2025.
Her committee assignments are Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation, Highways and Transit, and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees) and Science, Space, and Technology.
According to her House biography, she lives with her family in Rockville Centre.
